message.content: {"scores":{"c1":6,"c2":5,"c3":4},"evidence":"Word count is about 150, which is above the 70-130 range. It starts with 'what they are.', which completes the 'based on' clause grammatically. There are no statistics or personal anecdotes. The rural kid is a hypothetical rather than a fabrication. The overshoot is the main deduction on c1. On c2, the answer addresses differential pricing ('fast lane', 'telephone company charge a surcharge'), but it drifts into users being priced out ('rural kid', 'only people who get through are the ones who have the most to pay'). It does not explain why charging services differently harms competition or innovation, which partly conflates this with consumer pricing. On c3, the second paragraph is restatement ('You can get all the way back to that first point'). The prose includes quotable lines ('a new kind of segregation', 'two entirely different networks pretending to be one') and ends on a generic closer ('supposed to be open to everyone'). The essay's [1] footnote voice is loosely kept, but the development is thin."}
